documentation.range: Leptocereus wrightii is endemic to Cuba and is known from 10 plants on the outskirts of La Habana. The only previously known population disappeared during the development of the neighborhood of Villa Panamerica (Palmarola 2009). The species now occurs in a single location and its estimated area of occupancy is 4 km2 (a single grid cell of 2 x 2 km).
documentation.population: This species is possibly the most threatened cactus in Cuba. The last known plants grew in the coastal vegetation located between the neighborhoods of Camilo Cienfuegos and Cojimar (Habana del Este) and disappeared in 1992 during the development of the neighbourhood of Villa Panamericana. Recently 10 plants were discovered on the coast at Puerto Escondido, Havana city (Palmarola 2009). The population comprised of ten adult plants (Gonzalez-Torres et al. 2007).
documentation.habitats: This species grows in karstic rocks in the transition zone between the coastal thicket and the remains of a dry tropical forest (Gonzalez-Torres et al. 2009). Leptocereus wrightii is bat pollinated (Fleming et al. 2009).
documentation.threats: The main threats to this species are fire, damage by herbivores, and urban development (Gonzalez-Torres et al. 2007).
documentation.measures: There is no information on whether the area where this species was rediscovered has been protected. This species is being cultivated ex-situ and it has been re-introduced in Havana (Gonzalez-Torres et al. 2007). The places where it has been reintroduced are protected. The extant wild population has no regeneration of new plants, so close monitoring is needed.
documentation.use_trade: It is not known whether this species is used or traded.
documentation.rationale: This species is listed as Critically Endangered because it is known from one site (estimated area of occupancy is 4 km<sup>2</sup>) in the outskirts of Havana with only ten adult plants, and its population is continuously declining given that there is no regeneration of plants. Unless the natural habitat is restored, it is unlikely that the species will recover.
